newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX gasoline ends sharply up on supply concerns.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX gasoline ends sharply up on supply concerns.

text.p: NYMEX gasoline surged Monday to a settlement high for the prompt contract as refinery strikes in Europe threatened to decrease supply on top of a tight U.S. cash market, traders said.
"The cash market has been really strong, and there could be a supply decline," said a trader.

January gasoline ended up 2.66 cents a gallon at 68.12 cents, a closing high for the contract. January gasoline set an intraday contract high of 68.20. Riding gasoline's sizzling rally, January crude settled a sharp $1.05 a barrel higher at $24.80.

The strike by workers at three refineries of French oil giant Elf Aquitaine entered its fifth day. The stricken Elf plants make up a quarter of French capacity and three quarters of Elf's European refining network. The arbitrage from Europe to the United States for gasoline remains open, and the strike could lower imports, traders said.
Part of the steep gains in gasoline and crude was on technical buying, with stops triggered after 66.20 cents in Jan gasoline and after $24.40 in Jan crude, traders said.
Jan heating oil finished 1.89 cents a gallon higher at 73.57 cents.
Heating oil spent the first part of the session in negative territory, but was pulled higher by gains in gasoline and crude.
Traders noted volume was relatively slack throughout the oil complex, exaggerating price moves.

Spurring gains in crude was the shut down Monday of Mexico's three main crude ports due to bad weather, but officials at Cayo Arcas in the Campeche state said the port could soon reopen as winds have died down.
"At most, the port closures acounted for 20 cents of the $1.00 gain in crude," said Jim Ritterbusch, a trader with Sweeney Oil in crude.
Crude was also bolstered by reports that a U.N. committee is meeting Tuesday to discuss Iraqi oil smuggling.

But, the regulary scheduled meeting Tuesday by the U.N. sanctions committee on Iraq will discuss a variety of subjects, one of which is a four-month old charge by the United States that Iran aided Iraq in smuggling gasoil through Iranian waters, U.N. diplomats said.
The U.N. sources said the U.S. charges are unrelated to Iraq's oil-for-food deal.
-- Harry Milling, New York Energy Desk, 212-859-1761
